text:
Sam: handing primary to Jin for the 18:00-02:00 window. quick notes: incoming traffic spike yesterday, p99 risen to ~890ms on gen-prod, KV cache thrash suspected. i'm available on pager if anything weird.
Jin: thanks — taking it. do we have any open runbook actions i should start with?
Sam: top of list: check kv cache hit rate, restart inference-front if <50% hit, consider fallthrough to small-quant model for heavy tails. links below.
Maria: looping in incidentbot summary for the recent pager: incidentbot: [pager] gen-prod p99 elevated, 18:12 UTC, routes affected: text-gen-east-1. page_count: 12. severity: sev2.
incidentbot: recent actions: autoscale triggered at 18:15 (3 -> 6 pods), 1 pod failed startup and was restarted by k8s.
Alex: quick pointer — when you restart, use the graceful command to preserve KV: `kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/gen-front --grace-period=30` and monitor backlog.
Jin: noted. any smoke tests after restart?
Sam: run the smoke script in ops repo: 
```
./tools/smoke-checks/run_smoke.sh --route gen-prod --samples 5
```
should get <200ms on small samples or escalate.
Maria: runbook links: KV cache troubleshooting: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-stall 
Fallback model policy: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-fallbacks 
Graceful restart checklist: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/graceful-restart
(put these in your runbook notes)
Jin: thanks — i'm going to: 1) check hit rate dashboards, 2) verify 6 pods are healthy, 3) graceful restart front if hit rate <60%, 4) run smoke checks, 5) if still noisy, flip to small-quant fallback for 10m.
Sam: for flipping model: ops-bot can apply traffic split. example: `ops-bot apply-split --from gen-large --to gen-small-quant --pct 10 --duration 10m`
ops-bot: command acknowledged. requires oncall confirmation.
Jin: confirmed, i'll only run split after smoke fails.
Alex: if you see KV key errors, check redis metrics and run the eviction probe: `redis-cli -h redis-prod latency latest` and `redis-cli -h redis-prod info memory`. eviction thresholds: used_memory_rss > 0.9 * maxmemory -> purge candidates.
Maria: customer impact note: currently ~2% of requests are timing out (>10s) and are being retried by clients; escalate to sales only if >5% or sustained for 30m. log pointer: https://redwood.internal/logs/gen-prod?q=timeout
Jin: plan: i'll attempt graceful restart at +5m if hit rate low. will post updates here.
[10m later] Jin: did the graceful restart (rolled front) — pods restarted cleanly, KV hit went from 38% -> 62%. p99 dropped to ~420ms. running smoke now.
Sam: nice. watch for increase in 5xxs while caches warm.
Jin: smoke checks: 5/5 pass, median 110ms, p95 300ms. leaving autoscale at 6 for now.
Maria: recommend leaving note in incident tracker: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-489 with summary and commands used.
Jin: added notes and commands. leaving primary to Alex at 22:00. handoff checklist done.
Sam: handback acked. quick handoff tips for next oncall: - check kv hit rate first - run graceful restart instead of hard kill - have fallback split prepared and tested in staging - set a short monitoring window after restarts (10-15m)
Alex: acknowledged, thanks. tagging the runbook snippets in the rota doc for quick access. :thumbsup:
Maria: closing thread — small followup: i'll schedule a postmortem ticket if we see recurrence in 24-48h.
Sam: thanks team, leaving note in the handoff doc: https://redwood.internal/oncall/handovers/2026-03-15-jin -> Alex
Jin: signing off primary. ping me if pager goes off.
Alex: taking over.
